comment: One row for each rule of the report of part 1 of the leak rule of D17.20 for the locals of an
owning aggregate type (D17.7), which only reports until refinement R1: the obligation of each
exit kind and its exceptions, the facts of the owners below the local and the walk that tests
them, the verdict and its count, the limit of the aggregate work, and the cause of each exit
that the pass does not prove (src/fort/owner/prover.ft). Then the lines of the report
stage runs the cases over FIR text and over lowered fort source, the work limit and the lines
of the report (test/fort/owner/prover_aggregate_test.ft). The second runs the driver test, which
holds the option. The third runs the oracle test, which prints a false accept of the owning
aggregate locals for each row that makes the pass prove an exit that a run leaks at. The table
runs in the Linux VM with the debug preset and the default runner. The md5 guard reads the
product compiler, whose driver imports owner.prover and owner.report.
The first two rounds of a run can read stale (notes/testing.md 7), so the first two rows are
ones that a full run caught.

stages.name: the aggregate module test
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --root test/fort --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --timeout 1500 -j 2 owner/prover_aggregate_test

stages.name: the driver test
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --root test/fort --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --timeout 1500 -j 2 driver_test

stages.name: the oracle test
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --root test/fort --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --timeout 1500 -j 2 owner/oracle_test
